name: Bishop's Opening, Urusov Gambit
summary: The Urusov Gambit is a Bishop's Opening move order in which White offers the d-pawn for rapid development and a dangerous attack on f7.
intro: Reached via 1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 Nf6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nf3, the Urusov Gambit uses a Bishop's Opening move order to offer the d-pawn. In return White gains fast development and attacking chances against the f7-square, generating a strong initiative that can catch an unprepared opponent off guard.
line: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 Nf3

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: White's idea is speed: by conceding the d4-pawn, White develops the knight to f3, prepares O-O and Nxd4, and coordinates the c4-bishop with the queen against f7. The open lines and lead in development are the compensation, and Black's slightest inaccuracy can prove costly.

Black can choose between grabbing material and staying solid. Accepting fully with 4...Nxe4 5.Qxd4 hands White a powerful initiative and central queen, so Black must defend carefully and return material when appropriate rather than clutch every pawn.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: After 4...Nxe4 5.Qxd4, White's queen dominates the centre while the c4-bishop and rapid development create real threats; Black must untangle precisely, often with ...Nf6 and quick castling, to survive into a playable middlegame. This is the critical test of the gambit's soundness.

Alternatively, 4...Nc6 or 4...Bb4+ steer the game toward related open-game territory, and play can transpose into Two Knights Defense or Max Lange Attack structures. These transpositions let a well-prepared White player funnel Black into familiar attacking setups.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: The gambit is named after Prince Sergei Urusov, a strong Russian amateur and contemporary of Mikhail Chigorin in the nineteenth century, who analysed and championed the line. It has remained a favourite surprise weapon in club and correspondence play, prized for its sharp, initiative-driven character and its ability to sidestep heavily analysed main lines.
